newsitem.title: USA: Suspected car thief rescued from U.S. river.
newsitem.headline: Suspected car thief rescued from U.S. river.

text.p: A suspected car thief was hoisted to safety by daring rescuers off a tiny river island in Maryland on Wednesday after five hours of battling hypothermia, police said.

Police in Howard County, Maryland, outside Baltimore, said four suspects, including the driver, David Cook, 22, had fled from a stolen car after running into a dead-end street during a police chase early on Wednesday.

Although two suspects were immediately arrested, the other two got away. But police soon got a call that a man, who turned out to be Cook, was trapped on the island in Potapsco River and yelling for help.
Howard County Police Sergeant Dave Richards said a police officer and a fire fighter tried to wade out to Cook in cold, turbulent waters.

The officer made it but the firefighter got caught in the rope underwater, was cut free, and then floated downstream for about a quarter of mile until he was pulled out unconscious, said county Fire and Rescue Lieutenant Chris Cangemi.
Meanwhile a rescue team worked to set up a pulley system running from the shrub-covered island to a steep river bank.
Five hours later, Cook was placed on the line and hand-pulled across the river before he was taken into custody.
Cook was treated in a hospital for hypothermia and was being charged with theft, fleeing police and other charges, police said.
The firefighter who was swept downriver in the rescue attempt was treated at a hospital and discharged.
